english.title: Football - fail to comply with requirement re application for a banning order
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the subject of an application for a banning order under the Football Spectators Act 1989, failed to comply with a notice served on you by the police on **(..SPECIFY DATE..) under Section 21B of that Act in that **(..SPECIFY THE BREACH..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 21C(2) of the Football Spectators Act 1989.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
fails to comply with a notice
given to you under section 21B

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence wording is released pursuant to the Football (Disorder) Act 2000 which combines Domestic and International Football Banning Orders.
See also H4269 which remains in force in respect of a breach of a Restriction Order made under the Football (Offences and Disorder) Act 1999. Restriction Orders under Football Spectators Act 1989 became International Football Banning Orders and Domestic Football Banning Orders from 27/09/1999. Restriction Orders were made for a maximum of five years and therefore could remain in force until 26/09/2004.
(ii) See H3470 for Football Spectator failing to comply with a Banning Order made pursuant to the Football (Disorder) Act 2000, as incorporated into the Football Spectators Act 1989.
(iii) A section 21B notice will specify the time and date for appearance at court:(a) for hearing on an application
(b) a requirement not to leave England and Wales for that time.
(c) if it relates to a match outside the UK, to surrender his passport to the constable.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
